Source review + matched captures / 23 October 2026
Aurum 0.5.9 / codex branch

Same world.
Same camera.

Photon and Complementary now run in a separate client against the same saved terrain. Their source code and these captures guided a new pass on sunset shadows, surface light, fog, shafts and water.

Aurum is still below the reference level.

The changes fix concrete lighting and integration problems. The matched images still show a clear gap in atmospheric richness, foliage response, reflection detail and shaft definition. Intel UHD performance has not been measured here.

04 / Direct source review

Changes grounded in the rendering code

Photon's diffuse lighting, light colours and analytical/ray-marched fog were read directly, along with Complementary's surface/ambient colours, atmospheric fog and volumetric light. Aurum implements the relevant general techniques within its existing passes.

Finding0.5.9 implementation
Low-sun shadows faded earlyThe map now reaches full strength at sun-direction Y=0.08; the bounded shadow direction permits longer ground shadows.
Direct light and broad fill looked similarGolden-hour sky fill is reduced, direct light is modestly stronger, and rough solids use a restrained grazing diffuse wrap. Noon keeps its original cosine response.
Uneven ray segments had equal weightThe same ten shadow taps are weighted by segment length and front-to-back attenuation.
Fog and shafts were applied separatelyThey now use one forward-scattering response and one air opacity. Their composition runs in display-linear light, preserving more contrast than the old gamma-space glow.
Small plants never cast shadowsNearby grass, flowers and crops now cast within 8 blocks at 1024 shadow resolution, or 16 blocks with larger maps. Far small plants remain skipped; cached shadows do not track every wind movement.
Water deformed large reflection patchesBroad wave slopes are reduced further, with faster distance calming. Fine glitter and periodic coordinates are retained.
Integration check: a half-lit 60-block ray should measure 50% illumination. The old calculation measured 30%; the new ten-tap approximation measures 51%. With extinction, it stays within about one percentage point of the analytical test cases.

Source anchors: Photon diffuse lighting · Photon ray-marched fog · Complementary light and ambient colours · Complementary volumetric light.

05 / Method and practical limits

What this comparison proves

Controlled inputs

A copy of the saved world and options was used in a separate Fabric client with Iris 1.7.6 and Sodium 0.5.13. Camera, terrain, world time, vanilla textures, gamma 0.5, 12-chunk render distance and 1280 × 720 resolution match.

Clouds, mobs, animation and pack-specific sun paths differ. Aurum uses its custom settings with 1024-pixel shadows, a 64-block shadow range, blocky clouds and generated relief enabled.

Reference settings

Complementary used its source snapshot's HIGH profile without source changes. Photon used high with SH_SKYLIGHT disabled: the default compute program exceeded llvmpipe's 32 KB shared-memory limit. These are source snapshots, not claimed versioned releases.

Aurum ran on software OpenGL 3.3; the reference client used software OpenGL 4.5. This is an image comparison, not a speed benchmark.

CheckResultLimit
BuildPassedRemapped Fabric JAR produced. Repository unit-test task has no test sources.
GLSL + runtimePassedTerrain, composite and volumetric shaders validate; 14 Aurum programs compile in Minecraft.
Visual regressionReviewedVillage sunset, lake, open ocean, noon and night. Dedicated cave, rain and moving-camera acceptance remain open.
Intel UHD performanceUnmeasuredNo Intel GPU is attached. No UHD frame-time or 60 FPS claim follows from these tests.
Photon / Complementary qualityStill below targetMultiple scattering, full HDR colour cohesion, complete reflected environments and stronger motion reconstruction remain larger work.

The patch keeps the existing render-pass count and ten shadow samples per volumetric pixel. Nearby plant casters add bounded shadow-map rasterization. The additional arithmetic still needs target-GPU measurement. Aurum continues to render into an 8-bit scene through separate display paths; this patch does not provide full HDR composition.
